newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle close lower, feeders end mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle close lower, feeders end mixed.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed lower on fund liquidaton and disappointment over cash sales at $67.00 per cwt this week while feeder cattle futures closed mixed, influenced live cattle and corn futures, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.675 to 0.225 cent per lb lower led by June at 65.150 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.150 cent a lb higher to 0.300 lower with August off 0.175 at 77.300 cents.

Disappointment that packers paid $67 per cwt for cash cattle weighed on futures and knocked prices into fund sell stops, traders said. Many market watchers had expected cattle to sell at $68 this week, traders said.

"Next week is a short kill week and the packers are saying we don't need to be that aggressive," said Paul Georgy, president of agricultural consulting firm, Allendale Inc. "Retailers are basically done buying (beef) for this week and we have a short kill week next week."

Packers were expected to increase bids following reports of good weekend beef clearance at U.S. food stores and a firmer tone to boxed beef values Monday. But beef demand is also expected to decline as retailers may already have finished their purchases for the post holiday needs, including the start of supplying for Fathers Day in June, they added.

Fill-in business for after the Memorial Day holiday is likely finished by today (Tuesday). After Memorial Day is typically a weak demand period, except for Fathers Day, and "then it's into the dog days of summer" for beef demand, Georgy said.

Rosenthal Collins and Dean Witter sold June late while Cargill Investor Services and R.J. O'Brien bought after being on both sides early. E.D.&F. Man, Prudential Securities, Cargill and Lind-Waldock sold August while Refco bought, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, commission houses bought June 64 puts and commercials bought June 66 calls, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle futures followed the lead of live cattle most of the day, especially after the sharp break in the latest CME feeder cattle index, but recovered late when corn futures declined. Feeders were lower most of the day despite lower corn futures early, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index fell $1.31 to $76.33 per cwt.
ABN Amro-Chicogo Corp bought September late while mixed commission house buying pared the loss in August, traders said.
Cargill Investor Services spread long February live cattle/short February feeders, pit sources said.
